Once apprehended, the captor gains the ability to inspect the prisoner's belongings, set them free, or accompany them to an alternate area. Transporting escorted prisoners is also possible, including loading them into vehicles if needed. Depending on your settings, units may need to surrender before being taken captive.

%2Approach the unit and use the [%3%13%4].
%2The interaction is located around the hands in the form of a handcuffs icon.
%2Repeat to release."]["%3Cable Ties%4 enable a soldier to capture and detain another soldier. ["%3Chemlight Shields%4 give you the ability to read your map, even in dark environments. However, when using %3Chemlight Shields%4, you will have a slight glow around you.

%3Usage:%4
%2Use [%3%12%4] and select %3Equipment%4.

["The %3M1 Abrams%4 is a third-generation main battle tank developed by the United States after the failure of the MBT-70 project. Originally built around the M68A1 rifled tank cannon, the A1 revision switched to the German-built Rheinmetall L/44 120mm smoothbore cannon, produced under license as the M256A1.
All CUP Variants of the tank feature an additional M240 Coax gun, an M2 for the commander and an M240 for the loader. In addition, the TUSK variants feature a CSAMM (Counter-Sniper/Anti-Material Mount) with a barrel-mounted M2 .50BMG%1There is a total of nine different variants of the M1 available in CUP:
%2M1A1SA/AIM
%2M1A1SA TUSK
%2M1A1 FEP
%2M1A1 FEP TUSK
%2M1A2SEPv1
%2M1A2SEPv1 TUSK I
%2M1A2SEPv1 TUSK II
%2MBT P.H. Orlando
%2MBT P.H. Orlando (TUSK)
%1The %3M1A1FEP%4 (Firepower Enhancement Package) is mainly used by the USMC. Traditionally, only partial TUSK kits are installed and the rear side skirt flap is missing, but a full TUSK kit is also provided. The US Army operates both the M1A1 and M1A2. The M1A1 used is the %3SA/AIM%4 (Situational Awareness/Abrams Integrated Management) variant, a version of the A1 that is based on older versions and is completely rebuilt with new parts, among other things, a thermal sight for the commander. The %3M1A2SEPv1%4 is one of the latest developments and is also available to the NATO faction in the Arma 3 2035 scenario and features a very prominent independent Commander sight with a next-gen thermal imaging system. There are three variants, the normal SEPv1, the TUSK I kit with extra ERA armor blocks, and the TUSK II kit which has ERA on its ERA!
%1Finally, RACS, the Royal Army Corps of Sahrani, uses an export version of the M1A2 named the %3MBT P.H. Orlando%4, named after Crown Prince Orlando, the founder of modern-day Sahrani. The Orlando has most of the upgrades of the M1A2, but lacks the depleted uranium armour and therefore has worse armour all-around.
%1All CUP Abrams have a fully modelled interior, but the interior modelled is that of the M1A2 (except for the commander persicopes which differ between variants). Making a separate interior for the A1 would have been too much effort. The interior is supposed to be more or less like 'the real thing', although simplified."]["The %3M1 Abrams%4 is a third-generation main battle tank developed by the United States after the failure of the MBT-70 project. ["The M1 commander has his CDU (Commander Display Unit) in front of him. There are two screens on the CDU. The upper screen shows the view through the M2's weapon sight (M1A1) or the independent CITV Thermal Imaging camera in the A2. The screen can be switched through different vision modes with the %3%11%4 key binding. The lower screen shows some information on the tank, as well as a compass with separate pointers for the turret and commander optic/gun direction, as well as a full run-down of possible shells and how many of them are still available.%1The M1A1's commander gun is remote-controlled from the inside. On the M1A2, the gun is not remote controlled and the commander needs to turn out to be able to use it. Note that for consistency with the loader, the M1A2 M2 needs to be 'grabbed' via the action menu. Also note that on the M1A2 TUSK, the angle of movement is very limited due to the installed shields.
%1One peculiarity of the CUP Abrams is the ability of the commander to use the GPSE, the %3Gunner Primary Sight Extension%4. The GPSE allows the commander to look through the gunner's sight, and allows him to see what the gunner sees. The option is available on the action menu, as well as the optin to switch back to the commander's optic.
%1All crew positions can toggle the internal lights at night."]["The M1 commander has his CDU (Commander Display Unit) in front of him. There are two screens on the CDU. %1One peculiarity of the CUP Abrams is the ability of the commander to use the GPSE, the %3Gunner Primary Sight Extension%4. ["The M1 Abrams 120mm Smoothbore cannon has a wide variety of shells. This table lists all shells with some extra information. All ammunition for the M256 cannon is cased in a combustable shell casing that burns up during firing, leaving only the blast cap to be ejected from the cannon breach. A wide variety of shells is available. Dates are provided for historically accurate loadouts.

%3M829%4
In service since: 1984
Type: Armour - Piercing Fin - Stabilized Discarding Sabot Tracer(APFSDS - T)
Nominal Velocity: 1679 m/s%1Kinetic energy armour piercing anti - tank round intended for use with the M256 cannon. Uses a depleted uranium penetrator.


%3M829A1%4
In service since: 1991
Type: Armour - Piercing Fin - Stabilized Discarding Sabot Tracer(APFSDS - T)
Nominal Velocity: 1569 m/s%1Kinetic energy round, an upgrade of the M829.Nicknamed %3Silver Bullet%4 during the Gulf War


%3M829A2%4
In service since: 1992
Type: Armour - Piercing Fin - Stabilized Discarding Sabot Tracer(APFSDS - T)
Nominal Velocity: 1680 m/s%1Another iteration on the M829, this round uses a new manufacturing process to improve the stability of the penetrator.


%3M829A3%4
In service since: 2003
Type: Armour - Piercing Fin - Stabilized Discarding Sabot Tracer(APFSDS - T)
Nominal Velocity: 1555 m/s%1Little public knowledge is available on this round. The major upgrade to the A2 is an improved propellant charge and improved aerodynamics. In spite of weighing over 25 kg, the round still reaches 1555 m/s nominal speed.


%3M830A1%4
In service since: 1992
Type: High Explosive Anti-Tank Multi Purpose Tracer (HEAT-MP-T or MPAT)
Nominal Velocity: 1410 m/s%1A super-heated jet of molten copper ejects from the tip at impact, punching through light armour with no loss of penetration over range. The round is fired using a sabot and is fin-stabilized like APFSDS.


%3M908%4
In service since: 1984
Type: High Explosive Obstacle Reduction (HE-OR-T or MPAT-OR)
Nominal Velocity: 1140 m/s%1This round has a high-explosive warhead and is primarily used against buildings and unarmoured targets. Like most rounds fired from the M256, the warhead is fin-stabilized and fired using a sabot.


%3M1028%4
In service since: 2004/2005
Type: Canister

["The base model Su-25 in RHS is capable of launching several types of laser guided missiles such as the Kh-25, Kh-29, and S-25L. However, unlike default Arma 3 aircraft which use targeting cameras that people familiar with western aircraft might be used to, the basic model Su-25 in RHS has no such system in the real world or in game. Instead, it uses the Klen-PS laser designator located in the nose of the Su-25. Rather than being aimed by a camera, the Klen-PS is aimed through a crosshair located on the HUD whcih the pilot can move and lock to a specific point on the ground in front of the aircraft. The following is a basic firing proceedure using the Klen-PS:




1. With the nose of the aircraft pointed at a target, press the %11 key to turn on the Klen-PS laser. Once the laser is active, a green light located to the bottom left of the HUD will turn on.

2. With the laser now active, the targeting reticle can be locked to a specific point on the ground via the %12 key and moved around the HUD via the user 15-18 keybindings. If those keys are bound, they will show up below:
%2Move reticle left (User 15): %13
%2Move reticle right (User 16): %14
%2Move reticle up (User 17): %15
%2Move reticle down (User 18): %16

3. With the laser locked to the ground and/or pointed at the target, fire a guided missile. Continue pointing the nose of the aircraft in the general direction of the target until the missile impacts the target. Moving the nose of the aircraft beyond the gimbal limit of the laser designator will cause the Klen-PS to lose its lock on the targeted point.

4. After the missile has impacted the target, it is %3extremely important%4 to turn off the Klen-PS laser by pressing the %11 key again. The laser on the Klen-PS can only stay on for a maximum of 60 seconds, but it requires a cool down period that is directly proportional to how long the laser has been active. The cool down period can be anywhere between 15 seconds and 1 minute, depending on how long the laser was active.

["Targeting guided missiles in the A-10A is achieved through the television monitor (TVM) which provides a direct video feed from seeker located in the nose of the AGM-65 to the pilot of the aircraft. Essentially, you see exactly what the missile sees.

In order to use the TVM, switch weapons to an AGM-65 Maverick variant and press the %11 key to look through the TVM. Upon looking through the TVM, %3you will see a blank screen on the TVM%4. This is normal. In order to activate the TVM, you need to turn on the thermal seeker in the AGM-65 by pressing the %12 key. Once activated, the TVM should now function like any other targeting camera in Arma 3 with a few small differences:

1. While not looking directly through the TVM camera, the seeker of the Maverick can be slewed around the HUD and TVM using the user 15-18 keys. If you have those keys bound, you will see them mapped below:
%2Move seeker left (User 15): %13
%2Move seeker right (User 16): %14
%2Move seeker up (User 17): %15
%2Move seeker down (User 18): %16

2. Within the TVM, there is a cross that moves across the screen as the seeker moves around. This cross tells the pilot where the AGM-65 seeker is pointed in relation to the direction of the aircraft. When the cross reaches the edge of the TVM, that means the seeker has reached the gimbal limit of the seeker head. In addition, after pressing the stabilize turret key (%17), the cross will begin flashing to indicate that the camera/seeker is successfully locked and stabilized to the terrain it is pointing at.

3. With only one AGM-65 left, the camera feed will immediately cut as soon as the missile is fired. Since the seeker in the missile is what is acting as the camera for the pilot, once the missile leaves the rail, there is nothing left to serve as a feed for the TVM. For this reason, it is sometimes wise to save a single AGM-65 as an emergency only weapon, just so the pilot has a camera to spot and target ground vehicles with."]["Targeting guided missiles in the A-10A is achieved through the television monitor (TVM) which provides a direct video feed from seeker located in the nose of the AGM-65 to the pilot of the aircraft. ["There are three basic types of UAVs.

The middle sized ground UAV %3%11%4 can be used mainly as reconnaissance or fire support. Thanks to its transport ability, this UAV can help units to move away from a dangerous place.

The main purpose of a small quadrotor %3%12%4 is reconnaissance. It doesn't carry any weapons but is equipped with a laser designator for marking targets. Small size and excellent maneuverability are also its big advantages.

A bigger fixed-wing %3%13%4 can carry air-to-ground missiles or bombs and is also equipped with a laser designator. Greyhawk can be used as an attack unit, or in case of the unarmed variant, as a reconnaissance unit.
